rationale: Strong normative design and +28% national mediation growth reported in 2025, but certified judge-mediator scarcity, 30+30 day scheduling pressure, and low local success rates (14% in PN Palembang) require implementation and mediator-capacity upgrades.

25-day SLA and Rp500M cap (PERMA 4/2019) drove +68% growth in <Rp500M resolution, but mandatory physical-attendance and same-jurisdiction rules plus low UMKM legal literacy warrant targeted amendment and outreach.

Flagship digital transformation achieving 99.65% PN e-Court registration in 2023 and +30.84% YoY growth in 2025; requires court-level admin staffing parity, PA/regional catch-up, and UU 27/2022 PDP alignment.

Normatively strong CEDAW-aligned framework, but IJRS/Komnas Perempuan 5-province evaluation shows uneven judicial uptake and socialization; needs mandatory training, monitoring indicators, and UU 12/2022 TPKS harmonization.

PERMA 8/2022 successfully integrated e-Berpadu across police, prosecutors, and courts, but the enactment of UU No. 20 Tahun 2025 (new KUHAP, effective Jan 2026) requires formal coherence amendment and empirical outcome auditing.

Core access-to-justice pillar (22,748 Prodeo cases in LAPTAH 2025; 67.8% female Posbakum share at PA Purworejo), but requires ring-fenced/flexible DIPA Prodeo budget buffers, standardized Posbakum outcome reporting, and tighter digital integration with e-Court.

PERMA 13/2016 successfully enabled corporate criminal prosecutions (e.g., Putusan 3/Pid.Sus-TPK/2019/PN.Bgl), but UU No. 1 Tahun 2023 (Pasal 45-50) and the MA Criminal Chamber's 2026 Raperma require formal amendment to standardize culpability benchmarks, measurable fine formulas, and pre-trial asset-freezing safeguards.

Strong binding tri-jurisdictional environmental framework sustaining strict liability under Pasal 38(5), but requires stronger civil execution/attachment (sita jaminan) enforcement, open SIPP execution tracking, and harmonization with Putusan MK 119/PUU-XXIII/2025 on Anti-SLAPP.

PERMA 1/2002 has served for 24 years as Indonesia's sole class-action framework (through 2026 haze litigation No. 292/Pdt.G/2026/PN Ptk), but predates e-Court (PERMA 1/2019 jo. 7/2022) and requires amendment to enable electronic class notice/opt-out, clarify subgrouping and certification standards, and integrate SIPP tracking.

PERMA 1/2024 achieved 3,353 restorative-justice criminal cases in 2025, but UU No. 20 Tahun 2025 (KUHAP Baru, Chapter IV Pasal 79-88) now codifies statutory RJ across all criminal stages, requiring formal amendment plus SIPP/template enforcement to fix the 2.80% Pasal 21 citation compliance rate.
